import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_92/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_92/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Select only the columns needed for the target
# Target schema: ['type': string, 'ride_id': integer]
# Convert ride_id to integer (if not already)
result = joined[['type', 'ride_id']].copy()
result['ride_id'] = result['ride_id'].astype(int)

# Write to the target path without index
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_92/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_92/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_92/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by 'type' and count 'ride_id'
result = joined.groupby("type", as_index=False).agg({"ride_id": "count"})

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
result.columns = ["type", "ride_id"]

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_92/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
